original.full_text: Stop treating your AI strategy as a line item in your IT budget; you are currently watching the birth of the next utility grid. NVIDIA is currently orchestrating a $500B capital mobilization with Tier-1 asset managers like BlackRock and KKR to turn compute power into a permanent, investable asset class. This shift mirrors the historical rollout of electrical grids and fiber-optic networks. For Houston’s business ecosystem—where heavy industry and energy infrastructure are the lifeblood—this represents a tectonic shift in how we finance competitive advantage. Why does this transition from Opex to Capex change the game for you? It means AI is no longer a software experiment you can cancel next quarter; it is becoming a foundational industrial asset that requires long-term capital commitment. At Amplify Intelligence, Leon Coe has been advising local firms to stop looking for 'AI quick wins' and start treating compute capacity as a critical infrastructure requirement comparable to real estate or logistics networks. How do you survive this shift? You must decouple your operational spending from your strategic compute acquisition. If your board views AI as a variable IT cost, you will lose your competitive edge to incumbents who are already treating GPU clusters as long-term balance sheet assets. Infrastructure doesn't care about your quarterly earnings cycles. It only rewards those who claim their stake before the grid is fully locked down. Is your current AI deployment built to scale as a permanent asset, or are you still renting space in someone else's infrastructure?
